Where it began

Brydon Carse was born in Gqeberha, South Africa, on 31 July 1995. Cricket ran in the family: his father, James Carse, was a Zimbabwean cricketer who played county cricket in England for Northamptonshire. Brydon's British ancestry let him play in the English county game, and he joined Durham on a development contract in 2016.

That summer brought his first-class debut in the County Championship and 17 wickets, which earned him a two-year deal. Durham signed him for three more years in September 2018.

The player

His England chance came in unusual circumstances. In July 2021 England had to pick a whole new one-day squad to face Pakistan at short notice, and Carse was in it. He made his debut on 8 July and took five wickets in the third match of the series five days later. His first Twenty20 international, against New Zealand in August 2023, brought him 3 for 23 and the man of the match award.

His Test debut came against Pakistan at Multan in October 2024. On the second day he had Naseem Shah for his first Test wicket, and he finished the match with four. By November 2026 he had played 14 Tests and taken 58 wickets at 30.19, with a best of 6 for 42 and one ten-wicket match.

What made him special

Pace was the heart of it. Carse regularly bowled at around 91 mph, and in a one-day international against the Netherlands in 2022 his speed caught the eye. He was a useful fielder too, with 14 Test catches by November 2026.

With the bat he was more of a cheerful contributor than a run machine: 357 Test runs at 17.85, with a highest of 56. Even so, a fast bowler who can make a Test fifty is never unwelcome in the dressing room.

Away from the middle

In 2022 the Northern Superchargers signed him for The Hundred, and he was called into England's squad as a replacement during the 2023 World Cup.

And finally

Born in South Africa to a Zimbabwean cricketing father, Carse found his cricketing home at Durham. The county, it is fair to say, got good value from that development contract.
